description.plain:
Justin Bieber (born March 1, 1994) is a pop musician and recording artist, singer-songwriter and part-time actor. Since bursting onto the scene in 2008 (after being discovered on YouTube) he has taken the world by storm and divided opinion; selling 15 million albums worldwide, making two concert-documentaries, winning numerous awards, amassing 100 million Twitter followers, and being the most Googled person on Earth more than once.

On November 17, 2009, shortly after being discovered by Usher, Bieber released his first EP, My World. The project featured his first hit “One Time.” Bieber followed with his first album, My World 2.0, on March 19, 2010. The album contained the hit “Baby,” which was famously the most disliked video on YouTube until December 2017.

Before finishing his third studio album, Justin released a Christmas album on November 1, 2011.

Believe was released on June 15, 2012, and featured elements of dance and R&B music, unlike the teen-pop styles found in his previous works. The album included the international hits “Boyfriend,” “As Long as You Love Me.”, and “Beauty and a Beat.”

After his third album, and before his fourth, Bieber released the compilation album Journals.

His fourth full album Purpose was released on November 13, 2015, with the lead single “What Do You Mean” becoming his first number one hit on the Billboard Hot 100. He later followed it up with two more number ones, “Sorry” and “Love Yourself,” which cemented his success in the adult pop world.

“Love Yourself” managed to set a record for most weeks in the top ten after debuting in the top ten, breaking out of a multiple-way tie that included the likes of “Starships” by Nicki Minaj and his own “What Do You Mean” and “Sorry.”

On February 14, 2020, Bieber released Changes, his first project since 2015.

He was notably in a relationship with Selena Gomez between 2010 and 2013.  Since 2013, Justin Bieber and Selena Gomez dated on and off, before breaking up in March 2018. In July 2018, Bieber became engaged and later married to model Hailey Baldwin.

description.plain:
With the help of Benny Blanco, Justin Bieber and Ed Sheeran wrote this parting song to a past lover—it’s both bitter and caring. “Love Yourself” is not as uptempo as Bieber’s recent singles  “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry,” but the song still has a catchy, pop core.

As with Justin’s recent singles  “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry”, many listeners can’t help but think of Selena Gomez when they hear the track. On a recent interview on The Ellen Show though, Bieber named only three songs that are definitely inspired by his ex-girlfriend: “Mark My Words,” “What Do You Mean” and “Sorry.”. This doesn’t mean that the implied ex-lover is not Selena Gomez.

Given Ed Sheeran’s contribution, it’s likely an amalgam of Gomez and one of Ed Sheeran’s exes (Athina Andrelos? Nicole Scherzinger?), if the song is autobiographical at all.

The graffiti artwork for “Love Yourself” (Justin revealed the tracklist by posting pictures of the names of the tracks graffitied on walls all around the world) can be found in Oslo, Norway. This song premiered on Beats 1 Radio along with his Halsey collaboration “The Feeling.”

On November 14th, 2015 the official music video was released. Directed by Parris Goebel, it shows an arguing couple communicating by dancing around their house. The video stars renowned dancers, Keone and Mari Madrid.

On December 6th, 2016, it was announced that Justin Bieber’s single “Love Yourself” was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Song Of The Year and Best Pop Solo Performance

Fun Fact: On March 4th, 2016, Vanity Fair recruited renown African American actor, Morgan Freeman so he could recite the lyrics to this song in a witty and humorous way.

description.plain:
Capping off a year filled with public apologies, “Sorry” is an upbeat anthem about asking for forgiveness.

On its surface, the second single from Purpose seems to be an apology to a woman for making mistakes in a relationship—Bieber said the song is “a little bit” about his ex Selena Gomez. However, Bieber has also suggested that the song is intended to be a more general apology to the world for his mistakes.

On “Sorry,” Bieber collaborated with songwriters Julia Michaels and Justin Tranter (both of whom annotated the song on Genius). Michaels and Tranter also wrote six songs from Selena Gomez’s Revival album, including several songs rumored to be about Bieber.

“Sorry” was produced by Skrillex and BLOOD, and it incorporates elements of tropical house, an EDM genre that’s characterized by a bright sound and Caribbean or Latin influences. BLOOD explained the music’s meaning:

The vocal manipulations make an ambiguous sound and a moment later Justin replies, ‘Sorry.’ Justin’s vocal delivery and the triumphant key of the song gave the narrative a warm color. The beat is saying moving forward, and apologizing, can be exciting and fun.

“Sorry” premiered on UK radio station CapitalFM. It was posted on YouTube together with a dance video featuring New Zealand’s ReQuest Crew. The video, directed and choreographed by Parris Goebel, features a unique new dance style that Goebel calls “Polyswagg,” a style she says combines “sassy woman fire with aggressive inner strength.”

The song debuted at #2 on Billboard’s Hot 100 chart, blocked from the top spot by the debut of Adele’s “Hello.” However,  10 weeks after its debut, it finally reached #1, dethroning Adele’s smash hit.

description.plain:
“Yummy” is the lead single to Justin Bieber’s fifth studio album, Changes, and his first solo release since his fourth studio album, Purpose, released on November 13, 2015. Its release was accompanied by a lyric video, and an official music video that released at 12:00 PM EST on January 4th, 2020.

Yummy is a term used to describe something or someone that you find very attractive or appealing. Justin uses this term to describe his wife, Hailey Bieber, to which he is known for publicly gushing over. Whether it’s commenting on photos of her, or writing a poem for her, Justin always shows just how much he loves his wife.

The song, along with its release date, was announced on December 24, 2019, via a trailer, for his album on YouTube, which also played a snippet from the track.

Bieber continued teasing the track all day on January 2, 2020, the day before the track’s release. He tweeted a snippet from the track’s apparent music video, as well as another teaser of the track’s instrumental version.

Bieber continued teasing the track all day on January 2, 2020, the day before the track’s release. He tweeted a snippet from the track’s apparent music video, as well as another teaser of the track’s instrumental version.

description.plain:
Third and final promotion single off his third album Believe which was released on iTunes on June 11th, 2012.

The collaboration with an established rapper, Big Sean, surprised many people, but it seemed to work pretty well. “As Long As You Love Me” added up to Bieber’s new sound and showed he had become more mature.

The official music video for the song was released on August 1st, 2012. It features a little acting from Justin’s side; he wants to be with this girl, but her dad is against it and does all he can to break them up.

description.plain:
“Baby” is about breaking up with someone you love and still wanting them even after you’ve broken up. It’s the lead single off of Bieber’s debut album, My World 2.0. It debuted and peaked at number five on the Billboard Hot 100.

It is also one of Justin Bieber’s most popular songs of all time, with it being certified 12 times platinum by the RIAA; it was also an international smash hit, that included a #3 peak in the UK.

“Baby” was the most watched video ever on YouTube – until “Gangnam Style” surpassed it two years later.

description.plain:
https://twitter.com/kanyewest/status/709070533581774848

Justin first announced “What Do You Mean?” a month ahead of its release on Ryan Seacrest’s nationally-syndicated radio show.  When asked about the song’s meaning, Justin referred to the indecision and veiled sentiments he often heard when talking to women:

Girls are often flip-floppy. They say something, and then they mean something else. “What do you mean?“ … I don’t really know, that’s why I’m asking.

To build anticipation, Justin enlisted a series of celebrities to help count down and preview the song on Twitter. Nine days before the official release, Justin leaked the lyrics in “the coolest way ever” (according to MTV) by sending them in parts to his loyal fans (the Beliebers) via direct messages on Twitter.

https://twitter.com/justinbieber/status/634038239624478721

The unique marketing worked. “What Do You Mean?” become the fastest song to reach number one on iTunes after its release, and debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, the 23rd song ever to accomplish the feat.

Surprisingly, this was Justin’s first number one hit.

description.plain:
Justin Bieber reunites with Chicago rapper Chance the Rapper and kicks off a “new era” on “Holy,” a song that focuses on his love for his wife Hailey Baldwin. The track draws a parallel between the two lovers' relationship and the prescriptions stemming from both religion and outsiders. Chance contributes to the song with a verse focusing on maintaining faith and enjoying life.

“Holy” is Justin’s first solo single since his February 2020 fifth studio album Changes, and presumably serves as the lead single to his upcoming sixth studio album. The official music video was released on his YouTube channel alongside the song.

description.plain:
“Intentions” is the third single for Justin Bieber’s Changes album. The song’s lyrics are full of compliments towards both Bieber’s and Quavo’s love-interests: Hailey Bieber and Saweetie. Both artists express their intentions of caring for their women over a bright and happy beat. This song marks the third time that Justin Bieber and Quavo have worked together, with the previous two taking part in collaborations with DJ Khaled.

The song was previewed on a speculated tracklist along with several other tracks in the singer’s docu-series Justin Bieber: Seasons, which was officially released to YouTube on January 27, 2020. Later, the song was confirmed on Apple Music as track number 4 featuring Quavo.

description.plain:
Bieber shows us his soft, vulnerable side in this response to the highly visible mistakes he made over the course of his carrer up to this point.

With this new track, Justin wants to show everyone how he’s changed. Although he made mistakes, they were magnified by the fact that his every move has been at the center of the public eye since he was 14. With “I’ll Show You,” he explains that he never got the chance, like most teenagers, to mature outside the spotlight.

“I’ll Show You” is the second track the second off his fourth album Purpose, and it was released on November 1, 2015 as the third song to pre-order from the album. The video was shot in Iceland and was directed by Rory Kramer.

description.plain:
“Purpose” is a quiet piano ballad where Justin sings about his relationship with God—his newfound purpose in life—and sends a message of appreciation his Beliebers.

After years of personal struggles and media scrutiny, Justin’s found a new source of strength in his Christian faith, which he shares through the lyrics of “Purpose” and its spoken word outro.

Justin’s been candid about his beliefs in the past, but this is the first time his explicitly addresses them in his music.

description.plain:
The song was the first to be released from Bieber’s 2012 album Believe. It gained a lot of attention due to the sound — much different from Justin’s other material.

With “Boyfriend”, he proved that he wasn’t the innocent kid with a high pitched voice anymore: it marked the beginning of a new era for the singer. He got a new haircut as well and released the music video for the song, which shows him driving expensive cars and dancing with pretty girls in a way he hadn’t done before.

The new sound didn’t make him lose fans; Justin’s “Beliebers” had grown up as well and were ready for this more mature, yet still catchy and appealing music.

description.plain:
Justin Bieber’s first release of 2021 comes with “Anyone.” On this melodic song, he sings about his love for his wife Hailey Baldwin Bieber, expressing that he is and he will always be there for her regardless of anything.

The song was first performed live as part of Bieber NYE for New Year’s Eve at T-Mobile’s festival.

The official music video for the song premiered alongside the release of the song. In the video Justin imitates the famous boxer Rocky from the 1976 self-titled film, removing all of his tattoos. American actress Zoey Deutch, who is known for acting in the 2011 series, NCIS, stars as his lover in it.

description.plain:
Rumors of a collaboration between Bieber and Halsey began when Halsey contributed to the countdown to Bieber’s lead single, “What Do You Mean?” The song was finally announced on October 28th in a post on Bieber’s Instagram.

In an interview with MTV, Halsey confirmed that a music video (possibly previewed in this tweet) is in the works:

I’m terrified of giving away too much information. Imagine if I f–k up Bieber’s roll-out plan? There will definitely be a music video, given the song. It should be really, really interesting to see what people think when we put out a video. That’s all I can say.

“The Feeling” premiered on Beats 1 Radio on November 9th, 2015, alongside the Ed Sheeran co-written “Love Yourself.”

description.plain:
“No Pressure” is song about slowing down. The song features Justin crooning over an acoustic guitar loop accompanied by a heavy kick drum, droning bass and robotic stabs.

In this song, Justin is telling his ex-girlfriend that this time he is taking it slow, giving her time to clear her mind of the mistakes he did in the past. He realized how important this girl is for him and now he is willing to make up to her for all the pain that he put her through in their past relationship.

Under the pressure of the public eye, Justin has admittedly made mistakes.  He moved in with his then girlfriend, Selena Gomez, after only dating for three months. The two later went through a break-up. In 2014, he was arrested for a DUI while drag racing his Ferrari.

“No Pressure” marks the third official collaboration between Justin and rapper Big Sean; their first two being “As Long As You Love Me” and “Memphis,” both songs from his previous albums.

The official video was released November 14, 2015 and features black and white choreographed dancing.  It is part of a 13- track video playlist titled PURPOSE: The Movement.

description.plain:
On “Forever,” Justin Bieber reunites with Post Malone and recruits up-and-coming rapper and singer Clever. This marks the second collaboration between Bieber and Post, following Bieber’s feature on Post’s September 2016 single, “Deja Vu”, from Post’s debut studio album, Stoney, while this marks both Bieber and Post’s first collaboration with Clever.

The track is featured on Bieber’s fifth studio album, Changes.

The song was first teased on December 24, 2019, via a trailer for his album on YouTube, which played a snippet of the track. On January 4, 2020, over two minutes of the track leaked on song-sharing sites.

description.plain:
“Get Me” was a promotional single from Justin Bieber’s fifth studio album, Changes. It was released onto streaming at the same time as the album’s official title and cover art. On the track, Bieber and R&B singer Kehlani croon in a call-and-response format to each other about their figurative relationship and the two’s compatibility.

The track continues the R&B feel that Bieber has promised for his fifth studio album, with the duo singing very sexily over a very gloomy beat featuring many artificial percussion and bass that is trademark to the genre.

The track was initially teased the day prior to its official release on January 27, 2020, as it was shown on a potential track listing along with several other tracks in the singer’s docu-series Justin Bieber: Seasons.

description.plain:
“Changes” is by Justin Bieber, and is the title track, featured on his fifth studio album of the same name.

Billboard said about the track:

In the song Changes it actually talks about how some days we want to push further and some days we feel like doing nothing. And that often comes with a mood and an attitude towards life. Sometimes when life throws you things you can’t control and naturally your attitude is to be upset or to be disappointed or discouraged. But when you fight through those feelings that are just feelings in the end of the day you choose to put your effort into your work or into your passion and find that drive .. Life is worth living. And if you’re not going to give up the only thing to do is push forward.

Throughout the song, Bieber keeps the same subject, talking about different circumstances in life. His message states that he is going through changes, like he says in the chorus. In the outro, Bieber states that people change. An example of a change is the 2019-20 coronavirus pandemic in the world. However, at the time of this song’s release, it was not a pandemic.

description.plain:
“We Are” is a song by Justin Bieber featuring New York rapper Nas.

It had been rumored for a while that the two artists had been working on a song for Bieber’s new album Purpose, but when the tracklist of the album was revealed it was officially confirmed.

The song tells the story of a relationship, which is being destroyed by rumors and hate. As a famous singer, Justin is very familiar with people trying to create drama, especially when he is seeing someone. Dating can be difficult when you’re constantly being watched by everyone. The relationship Justin had with Selena Gomez was exactly like this. The song may even be inspired by it.

description.plain:
The sixth installment of Justin Bieber’s Music Mondays — where he released a track a week for ten weeks from his upcoming album Journals. These songs are supposedly from his personal journals and talk about his relationships — especially his two year romance with Selena Gomez. In “All Bad” he’s out here trying to salvage his rep with his girl.

All Bad was released November 11th, 2013, but Justin was feeling sick in Argentina earlier in the day and ended up going to the hospital after his show, so he couldn’t do a Twitter countdown this track.

Earlier in the year, the demo version of the song leaked which was written and performed by Poo Bear—who has assisted Bieber on the hit “Where Are  Ü Now”—with Justin singing the chorus; but with the release of Purpose, Justin now sings the whole song with added production in the form of a bouncy beat in the chorus.

description.plain:
On this sultry remix of Drake’s “One Dance,” Bieber uses Drake’s flow and some of his lyrics, while putting his own twist on others. He replaces Hennessy on the hook with 1942, a premium Tequila made by Don Julio, the same Don Julio he mentioned on Travi$ Scott’s “Maria I’m Drunk.”

This song was teased during a party in Monaco the weekend before it dropped. It marks the third time Justin has remixed one of Drake’s hits. Last year, he remixed “Hotline Bling,” and in 2013 was part of the “Trust Issues” remix.

The song premiered on OVO Sound Radio Episode 23.

description.plain:
‘Trust’ is a song by Justin Bieber on the deluxe edition of his highly-awaited, new studio album Purpose.

It has a R&B kind of vibe to it, like on Bieber’s previous album Journals.

Purpose is a combination of multiple music genres and it works surprisingly well. The fans who really enjoyed Journals, will probably like ‘'Trust’‘: it has the same type of feeling.

‘'Trust’‘ is about a relationship, where the person Justin is with isn’t so sure if they want to stay together.

Biebs is trying to convince them to listen to their heart and do what they feel like is the best thing to do, rather than what they think is the best option.

description.plain:
Continuing his transformation from teenage pop heartthrob into mature R&B singer, Justin teased a remix of Drake’s massive hit “Hotline Bling” on October 30th, 2015. Staying true to the themes of the original song, the remix was released in the style of a voicemail message, with Justin tweeting a phone number for fans to call and listen to the track.

https://twitter.com/justinbieber/status/660185702651461632

Justin’s version of the song tells a different story than the original, where Justin confronts a girl about keeping him and a romantic competitor both on speed-dial. Songwriter Poo Bear explained:

We rewrote it to make it be more like him and Drake dating the same girl, and then him finding out and actually talking to the girl, like, ‘I know you called him on his cell phone. We decided, let’s remix it so this girl knows she’s not going to come between two friends.

A few days before releasing this remix, Justin recreated his Canadian brother’s viral dance moves while visiting the UK’s Capital FM Radio Station.

description.plain:
Yet another JustinxSkrillex collab, “Children” is about making a positive impact in the world.

The two artists worked together quite a few times in 2015, when the song was released. For example, Justin features on the smash hit “Where Are Ü Now?” by Jack Ü, a duo which Skrillex is part of. description.plain:
“All In It” is a song by Justin Bieber on the deluxe edition of his highly anticipated album Purpose. Justin mentioned the song during a radio interview earlier this year.

The song is about doing what you love — something which is very important to Justin. In the spoken outro, he mentions his competitive personality as well as his love for God, a theme that comes back in several other songs on the album. What Bieber says about being competitive is very similar to what he said in his interview with Complex, a few weeks before the release of Purpose:

Growing up, I literally got my identity through being good at stuff. I always wanted to be the best because I felt like that’s how I got my self-worth.

description.plain:
“Home to Mama” is an acoustic duet between boy pop stars Justin Bieber and Cody Simpson. It’s a straightforward love song about falling in love with a girl and forming a long-term relationship.

However the timing of it’s release has caused some people to speculate whether it is about Selena Gomez, who just last week debuted her single “The Heart Wants What It Wants”, which delved into her relationship with Justin.

‘'Home To Mama’‘ is also on the Japanese edition of Bieber’s highly-awaited album Purpose.

body.plain:
“That’s What Love Is” is the fifteenth song on Justin Bieber’s fifth studio album, Changes.

On the track, Bieber sings with a backing guitar instrumental about how much he admires the “greatness” that comes with being in a relationship, and how he has learned from being in love.

description.plain:
A collaboration between Justin Bieber and Selena Gomez came as a surprise given their supposed breakup and their many subtle references to each other in past hits.

The song premiered on Drake’s OVO Sound Radio as an untitled track, but people think this track’s name is “Strong” because of the chorus.

Seventeen Magazine reported that an anonymous source claims that Bieber and Gomez recorded the duet about 3 years ago when they were still dating, “just for fun.”

The song didn’t appear on any album, neither Justin Bieber’s nor Selena Gomez’s.

description.plain:
“Hit the Ground” could possibly refer to the way Justin has felt over the past few years, when he got a lot of negative media attention, got arrested a couple times and had the wrong friends.

It was a difficult time for him, but Justin is doing a lot better now. It seems like on this track, he describes the way it felt to get so much hate over him on such a young age – it’s the story from his perspective in which he shares his most honest feelings.

‘'Hit The Ground’‘ is only on the Japanese edition of Purpose.

“All Around the World” is a song by Justin Bieber from his third studio album, Believe. The song was released as the final single from the album and marks the second collaboration between Bieber and Ludacris, having previously collaborated on “Baby” in 2010.

Breathy vocals swirl around a beat that pierces the listener on first contact. Ludacris wraps in double-time as the album’s electronica obsession is immediately presented.

description.plain:
Colombian reggaeton star J Balvin joins Justin for the Latino remix of “Sorry.”

Balvin and Justin had met before in Colombia in 2015—he taught him how to say “parcero,” a local Colombian word, similar to saying “friend” or “homie.”

In a profile published by The FADER, J Balvin discusses working with Bieber’s go-to songwriter Poo Bear—they recorded demos for Balvin’s upcoming album, Ninjas. Balvin hopes that one day Bieber will take the leap and sing Spanish on one of his tracks.

While J Balvin is one of the biggest stars in Latin America, he remains relatively unknown in America. He told The FADER:

I want to keep making history in Spanish. I want to invite the mainstream into my world, and to my sound, and to what I’m doing. And I want mainstream artists to respect me, and accept Latino artists as equals, without us having to sing in English.

description.plain:
“Die in Your Arms” is a song by Canadian recording artist Justin Bieber, from his third studio album, Believe (2012).

The track was written and produced by Rodney “Darkchild” Jerkins, Dennis “Aganee” Jerkins, and Travis Sayles, while additional lyrics were written by Bieber, Thomas Lumpkins, Kelly Lumpkins, and Herb Rooney. The R&B song samples Michael Jackson’s “We’ve Got a Good Thing Going” (1972), and lyrically, features Bieber singing about an all-consuming passion and the affection that he feels for his love interest.

“Die in Your Arms” received mostly positive reviews from music critics, who compared the song’s style to the ones of Jackson 5, Duffy and Bruno Mars, among others. The song has charted in several countries such as Australia, Canada, Netherlands, New Zealand, United Kingdom, and United States.

description.plain:
In an interview in November 2009 with Billboard, Justin stated:

It’s a ballad about the feelings I had when my parents split up and how I helped my family get through it. I think a lot of kids have had their parents split up, and they should know that it wasn’t because of something they did. I hope people can relate to it.

During a performance in Cincinnati, Ohio in 2010, whilst performing this song Justin broke down into tears.

description.plain:
“Always” is a currently unreleased track from Canadian singer-songwriter Justin Bieber.

The track has not yet been released, and it was leaked on December 4, 2019. It was later previewed by Justin in the second and fourth episodes of his YouTube exclusive documentary series; Justin Bieber: Seasons. The track’s title is unconfirmed and it is unknown if this track will make the final cut for Justin’s next album.

description.plain:
Justin is no stranger to “love” or “one” metaphors, but in “One Love”, he combines them to make a more mature song about embracing his sexy, yet monogamous relationship.

“One Love” is included as the 11th track on Believe, his fourth album. In fact, the first ten songs before this are all also about love. Perhaps they’re all about this same one love–like Selena Gomez?

description.plain: In this song, Justin is explaining how he puts up a wall around him. Yellow meaning happiness,  rain meaning the fame, the money, the girl and the bad times; the coat meaning a brick wall. In other words, he puts on the yellow raincoat to appear happy to the outside world. But once it is off, he is sad again. The raincoat keeps him safe to everything that is happening around him.

description.plain:
“Better Without You” is an unreleased song by Justin Bieber, which leaked online on June 24th, 2017.  An alternate version of the song, with a more R&B feel to it with the same lyrics, is titled “Better" and can be heard here

The song is said to be about Bieber and his then girlfriend at the time Selena Gomez' dying relationship. Throughout the song, Bieber is unsure what to do in the relationship, and ends up coming to terms that he’s much better off without her.

The complete version of song leaked on October 25th, 2017 on Twitter.

A day after the leak, the producer uploaded a first version of the song on his SoundCloud.

description.plain:
“Common Denominator” is a bonus track off the My World EP.

In mathematics, the denominator refers to the number at the bottom of a fraction. In order for two fractions to be added (or subtracted) they need to have the same denominator which is referred to as the common denominator.

In this song, Justin uses the common denominator as a metaphor for how this girl has changed things for him and allowed him to fall in love.

The use of elementary mathematical metaphors highlights that Justin his still young and new to love and points to his innocence at this phase in his songwriting and career.

description.plain:
Third and final promotion single off his third album Believe Acoustic which was released on iTunes on June 11th, 2012.

The collaboration with an established rapper, Big Sean, surprised many people, but it seemed to work pretty well. “As Long As You Love Me'‘ added up to Bieber’s new sound and showed he had become more mature.

The official music video for the song was released on August 1st, 2012. It features a little acting from Justin’s side; he wants to be with this girl, but her dad is against it and does all he can to break them up.

description.plain:
“Better” is an unreleased song by Justin Bieber, which leaked online on June 24th, 2017. The song has somewhat of an R&B feel to it. An alternate version of the song, with a more acoustic feel to it and with the same lyrics, is titled “Better Without You” and can be heard here.

The song is said to be about Bieber and his then girlfriend at the time Selena Gomez' dying relationship. Throughout the song, Bieber is unsure what to do in the relationship, and ends up coming to terms that he’s much better off without her.

description.plain:
On “La Bomba,” Justin Bieber reunites with Colombian reggaeton singer J Balvin, on a track on which they sing about dancing, as well as drop references to fashion designers.

On February 11, 2020, three days before Bieber released his #1 fifth studio album, Changes, he did a Q&A session with fans about the album. When a fan asked him about the placement of “La Bomba” on Changes, he confirmed its placement on his forthcoming sixth studio album.

A snippet of this track was played on January 27, 2020, on the first season and third episode of Bieber’s documentary series, Seasons. On February 28, 2020, a small part of the shooting of the music video was revealed.

Rallying celebrities around your new release is becoming pretty popular: Taylor Swift did it with multiple posters on Twitter for her “Bad Blood” music video, and Madonna followed suit for her “Bitch I’m Madonna.”

We have the full list of all celebrities counting down to Justin Bieber’s “What Do You Mean?” release.

body.plain: “Just Like Them” brings the retro vibe many recent pop songs have acquired the year of its release, 2012, including Bruno Mars' “Treasure” and the smash hit “Blurred Lines” by Robin Thicke. It conveys Bieber’s frustrations when a girl who was different from his exes begins acting like them, making him worry about the future of their relationship.

description.plain:
“Running Over” is a track by Justin Beiber, which had a recorded verse by Florida rapper Ski Mask the Slump God however the official version instead features Philadelphia rapper Lil Dicky.

The leak was uploaded to SoundCloud thanks to Gio, a friend of Ski Mask and DJ Scheme. He uploaded the song to his page with the description “ORIGINAL VERSE LMAO” and with the tag “#LOL LIL DICKY?”.

You can view the leaked song here.

description.plain:
Justin Bieber has apparently remixed Michael Jackson’s Slave to the Rhythm to include his own vocals!

Slave to the Rhythm was reportedly recorded by MJ just before his tragic death in 2009.
A heavier dance beat and Justin Bieber’s contributions have been added, of course, making for a monster collaboration of unknown origin and authenticity.

It’s unclear whether this remix was meant to be officially released, or if it’s a fan creation, though Justin’s tweets give the impression that it’s legitimate.

description.plain:
On October 10, 2019, Justin posted a series of videos on his Instagram story of him in the studio with his wife Hailey Bieber.

In one of the videos, you can hear Justin rapping to the beat of 50 Cent’s 2003 hit, “Many Men”.

Justin later said that the track was just him “messing around”, and that it wasn’t “album stuff”, so we probably won’t see this song on his upcoming album, if he has one in the coming years.

description.plain: “Baby” is a song by Canadian recording artist Justin Bieber. It was released as the lead single from the latter half of Bieber’s debut album, My World 2.0. The track was written by Bieber with Christopher “Tricky” Stewart and Terius “The-Dream” Nash, both of whom worked with Bieber on “One Time”, and also by R&B singer Christina Milian and labelmate, rapper Ludacris.

body.plain: Justin Bieber issues an apology for making a racist joke in a 5-year-old video clip that was widely circulated online.

songs.lyrics:
As a young man, I didn't understand the power of certain words and how they can hurt. I thought it was ok to repeat hurtful words and jokes, but didn't realize at the time that it wasn't funny and that in fact my actions were continuing the ignorance

Thanks to friends and family I learned from my mistakes and grew up and apologized for those wrongs. Now that these mistakes from the past have become public I need to apologize again to all those I have offended

I'm very sorry. I take my friendships with people of all cultures very seriously and I apologize for offending or hurting anyone with my childish and inexcusable mistake. I was a kid then and I am a man now who knows my responsibility to the world and to not make that mistake again

Ignorance has no place in our society and I hope the sharing of my faults can prevent others from making the same mistake in the future. I thought long and hard about what I wanted to say but telling the truth is always what's right

Five years ago I made a reckless and immature mistake and I'm grateful to those close to me who helped me learn those lessons as a young man. Once again.... I'm sorry

description.plain:
With the help of Benny Blanco, Justin Bieber and Ed Sheeran wrote this parting song to a past lover—it’s both bitter and caring. “Love Yourself” is not as uptempo as Bieber’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry,” but the song still has a catchy, pop core.

As with Justin’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry”, many listeners can’t help but think of Selena Gomez when they hear the track. On a recent interview on The Ellen Show though, Bieber named only three songs that are definitely inspired by his ex-girlfriend: “Mark My Words,” “What Do You Mean” and “Sorry.”. This doesn’t mean that the implied ex-lover is not Selena Gomez.

Given Ed Sheeran’s contribution, it’s likely an amalgam of Gomez and one of Ed Sheeran’s exes (Athina Andrelos? Nicole Scherzinger?), if the song is autobiographical at all.

The graffiti artwork for “Love Yourself” (Justin revealed the tracklist by posting pictures of the names of the tracks graffitied on walls all around the world) can be found in Oslo, Norway. This song premiered on Beats 1 Radio along with his Halsey collaboration “The Feeling.”

On November 14th, 2015 the official music video was released. Directed by Parris Goebel, it shows an arguing couple communicating by dancing around their house. The video stars renowned dancers, Keone and Mari Madrid.

On December 6th, 2016, it was announced that Justin Bieber’s single “Love Yourself” was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Song Of The Year and Best Pop Solo Performance

Fun Fact: On March 4th, 2016, Vanity Fair recruited renown African American actor, Morgan Freeman so he could recite the lyrics to this song in a witty and humorous wayhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRKZh-2j4PY

description.plain:
“Where Are Ü Now” is a Bieber ballad turned forward-looking EDM anthem thanks to Jack Ü’s production. Intimate, ornamented verses give way to driving, elastic drops with emotive melodies abound. Justin successfully showcases an updated vocal affect, his feigned sincerity reaching a pleasing, sentimental impact.

The production of Skrillex and Diplo as the duo Jack Ü bring together a unique collection of their distinctive production vocabularies, exhibiting masterful restraint and attention to detail in fashioning this very up-to-date, left field crossover.

The New York Times recently released a video interview with the three artist that details the making of the song.

Though “Where Are Ü Now” is officially Jack Ü’s song, featuring Bieber, it will be on the deluxe version of Justin’s new album Purpose as well.

The song won Best Dance Recording at the 58th Annual GRAMMY Awards.

Bieber shows us his soft, vulnerable side in this response to the highly visible mistakes he made over the course of his carrer up to this point.

With this new track, Justin wants to show everyone how he’s changed. Although he made mistakes, they were magnified by the fact that his every move has been at the center of the public eye since he was 14. With “I’ll Show You,” he explains that he never got the chance, like most teenagers, to mature outside the spotlight.

“I’ll Show You” is the second track the second off his fourth album Purpose, and it was released on November 1, 2015 as the third song to pre-order from the album. The video was shot in Iceland and was directed by Rory Kramer.

description.plain:
With the help of Benny Blanco, Justin Bieber and Ed Sheeran wrote this parting song to a past lover—it’s both bitter and caring. “Love Yourself” is not as uptempo as Bieber’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry,” but the song still has a catchy, pop core.

As with Justin’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry”, many listeners can’t help but think of Selena Gomez when they hear the track. On a recent interview on The Ellen Show though, Bieber named only three songs that are definitely inspired by his ex-girlfriend: “Mark My Words,” “What Do You Mean” and “Sorry.”. This doesn’t mean that the implied ex-lover is not Selena Gomez.

Given Ed Sheeran’s contribution, it’s likely an amalgam of Gomez and one of Ed Sheeran’s exes (Athina Andrelos? Nicole Scherzinger?), if the song is autobiographical at all.

The graffiti artwork for “Love Yourself” (Justin revealed the tracklist by posting pictures of the names of the tracks graffitied on walls all around the world) can be found in Oslo, Norway. This song premiered on Beats 1 Radio along with his Halsey collaboration “The Feeling.”

On November 14th, 2015 the official music video was released. Directed by Parris Goebel, it shows an arguing couple communicating by dancing around their house. The video stars renowned dancers, Keone and Mari Madrid.

On December 6th, 2016, it was announced that Justin Bieber’s single “Love Yourself” was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Song Of The Year and Best Pop Solo Performance

Fun Fact: On March 4th, 2016, Vanity Fair recruited renown African American actor, Morgan Freeman so he could recite the lyrics to this song in a witty and humorous way.

description.plain:
With the help of Benny Blanco, Justin Bieber and Ed Sheeran wrote this parting song to a past lover—it’s both bitter and caring. “Love Yourself” is not as uptempo as Bieber’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry,” but the song still has a catchy, pop core.

As with Justin’s recent singles “What Do You Mean?” and “Sorry”, many listeners can’t help but think of Selena Gomez when they hear the track. On a recent interview on The Ellen Show though, Bieber named only three songs that are definitely inspired by his ex-girlfriend: “Mark My Words,” “What Do You Mean” and “Sorry.”. This doesn’t mean that the implied ex-lover is not Selena Gomez.

Given Ed Sheeran’s contribution, it’s likely an amalgam of Gomez and one of Ed Sheeran’s exes (Athina Andrelos? Nicole Scherzinger?), if the song is autobiographical at all.

The graffiti artwork for “Love Yourself” (Justin revealed the tracklist by posting pictures of the names of the tracks graffitied on walls all around the world) can be found in Oslo, Norway. This song premiered on Beats 1 Radio along with his Halsey collaboration “The Feeling.”

On November 14th, 2015 the official music video was released. Directed by Parris Goebel, it shows an arguing couple communicating by dancing around their house. The video stars renowned dancers, Keone and Mari Madrid.

On December 6th, 2016, it was announced that Justin Bieber’s single “Love Yourself” was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Song Of The Year and Best Pop Solo Performance

Fun Fact: On March 4th, 2016, Vanity Fair recruited renown African American actor, Morgan Freeman so he could recite the lyrics to this song in a witty and humorous way.

On November 14th, 2015 the official music video was released. Directed by Parris Goebel, it shows an arguing couple communicating by dancing around their house. The video stars renowned dancers, Keone and Mari Madrid.

On December 6th, 2016, it was announced that Justin Bieber’s single “Love Yourself” was nominated for two Grammy Awards: Song Of The Year and Best Pop Solo Performance

Fun Fact: On March 4th, 2016, Vanity Fair recruited renown African American actor, Morgan Freeman so he could recite the lyrics to this song in a witty and humorous way.

description.plain:
‘Trust’ is a song by Justin Bieber on the deluxe edition of his highly-awaited, new studio album Purpose.

It has a R&B kind of vibe to it, like on Bieber’s previous album Journals.

Purpose is a combination of multiple music genres and it works surprisingly well. The fans who really enjoyed Journals, will probably like ‘'Trust’‘: it has the same type of feeling.

‘'Trust’‘ is about a relationship, where the person Justin is with isn’t so sure if they want to stay together.

Biebs is trying to convince them to listen to their heart and do what they feel like is the best thing to do, rather than what they think is the best option.

description.plain:
“Purpose” is a quiet piano ballad where Justin sings about his relationship with God—his newfound purpose in life—and sends a message of appreciation his Beliebers.

After years of personal struggles and media scrutiny, Justin’s found a new source of strength in his Christian faith, which he shares through the lyrics of “Purpose” and its spoken word outro.

Justin’s been candid about his beliefs in the past, but this is the first time his explicitly addresses them in his music.
